campos.mudanca: Updated information of the health risks you’ll face in Taiwan (‘Health’ page).

texto:
The UK does not recognise Taiwan as a state and has no diplomatic relations with Taiwan, so limited support is available to British nationals. Please refer to the British Office in Taipei for further information.
Typhoon season warning
Typhoons can affect Taiwan in June, but the most active period is between July and September. Typhoon frequency gradually decreases in October. If you are planning to visit Taiwan during typhoon season, it is important to stay informed and plan ahead:
monitor official weather forecast: check the website of the Taiwan Central Weather Administration for updated typhoon news
be flexible with your itinerary: flights, trains, buses and other transportation services may be delayed or cancelled during severe weather
check your travel arrangements with your travel provider
follow the guidance of the Taiwanese authorities
conditions may be dangerous for swimming, water sports and other activities in coastal waters around Taiwan during this period
Information and advice on how you can prepare for a range of disasters and emergency situations in Taiwan can be found in their Public Safety Guide or “Little Orange Book” .
Before you travel
No travel can be guaranteed safe. Read all the advice in this guide. You may also find it helpful to:
see general advice for women travellers
read our guide on disability and travel abroad
see general advice for LGBT+ travellers
read about safety for solo and independent travel
see advice on volunteering and adventure travel abroad
Travel insurance
If you choose to travel, research your destinations and get appropriate travel insurance . Insurance should cover your itinerary, planned activities and expenses in an emergency.
About FCDO travel advice
The Foreign, Commonwealth & Development Office ( FCDO ) provides advice about risks of travel to help British nationals make informed decisions. Find out more about FCDO travel advice .
